newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodia's Rainsy free after brief Thai detention.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Rainsy free after brief Thai detention.

text.p: Thai immigration officials released Cambodian opposition leader Sam Rainsy on Wednesday after briefly detaining him as he tried to enter Cambodia's western Poipet town, witnesses said.
"I will go back to Bangkok now," said Sam Rainsy soon after his release. He added that he had been detained by Thai authorities who feared for his safety.

Sam Rainsy was held as he attempted to cross the border into Poipet, a town controlled by royalist forces loyal to ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, to meet members of his Khmer Nation Party (KNP) who had fled Phnom Penh fearing repression from Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
Earlier this month, Hun Sen ousted Ranariddh and took control of the government in Phnom Penh by violently crushing the deposed prince's forces.

Sam Rainsy came to the Thai-Cambodian border on Tuesday. He said he had met Ranariddh in France and had agreed to join with the prince's FUNCINPEC party to resist Hun Sen's takeover of the Cambodian government through what he called illegal means.
He was detained as he tried to slip into Poipet to meet 52 members his party, who with about 300 others from Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party, are holed up waiting to flee the country.

A Thai army officer said Sam Rainsy's detention was initiated by the army, which then handed him over to immigration officials. The officer said Sam Rainsy had caused trouble for Thailand by using Thai soil to call for an uprising against the Cambodian government.
"He has caused trouble for Thailand and has used Thai soil to wage a campaign against the Cambodian government," the army officer said.

On hand to give assistance to the Cambodian opposition leader, who holds a French passport, was a representative of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, Pascal Meyer, a roving protection officer.
Later, Sam Rainsy said he had information that one of Ranariddh's top military commanders, General Nhiek Bun Chhay, was safe in Poipet.
The general disappeared after Hun Sen's forces crushed royalist forces in Phnom Penh earlier this month.

"I received a report form my source yesterday that he (Nhiek Bun Chhay) was approaching Poipet and today I got confirmation he has already arrived in Poipet and is safe under the protection of royalist forces," he added. "This is a big boost for the royalist forces.
